summary: Feed s126_double to SIEM is degraded: 9.3% duplicate packets (265/2858) and 2.2% TCP packet drops (61/2798) detected. Other checks (one-way, VLAN, encryption, oversize, truncated, tunnel, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating the same traffic from multiple SPAN/mirror sources (or both sides of a link) without deduplication - consistent with 'double' feed name. 9.3% duplicates exceeds 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM wastes storage, license and processing on duplicate events, inflates counts and correlation logic, and reduces fidelity. SIEM does not need both directions/full payload, so detection still functions but with noise and inefficiency.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within a short window before forwarding to the 1G SIEM port, eliminating double-counting without losing unique events.

findings.root_cause: Upstream SPAN/mirror or packet broker is dropping packets under load - 2.2% of TCP packets show gaps vs 1% threshold. Tool overload is healthy, so loss occurs before the SIEM, typical of SPAN buffer overflow or broker oversubscription.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives incomplete TCP streams and missing events, causing broken flow reassembly, incomplete logs and potential missed correlations/detections.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN/mirror with passive TAP and verify broker buffering/bandwidth to eliminate pre-tool drops. If TAP already in use, tune broker buffers and consider load_balance to prevent drops.
